changelog: - **The billable active matched pair now has exactly one definition, plus a nightly usage rollup and video volume counted** (#1750). "How many active pairs does this tenant have?" was answerable three slightly different ways — none of them the published one — and the nearest thing to a billing number (`planGate`'s `status: 'ACTIVE'` count) has no activity requirement, so a dormant pair counted and an invoice built on it would over-bill. The rule is now written once, in dependency-free `src/lib/meteringRules.ts` (unit-tested, `npm run test:metering`) with its queries in `src/lib/metering.ts`: *a relation in ACTIVE state with any logged activity in the calendar month; paused, benched and completed pairs are not counted* — the pricing-page sentence verbatim, as the module's header comment and as an exported constant. Billable states live in ONE allowlist (`BILLABLE_RELATION_STATES`), so a future `PAUSED`/`BENCHED` state is excluded automatically instead of needing seven queries edited; activity is one query with `some` filters over the seven per-relation signals (interaction log, message, meeting, meeting request, stage change, weekly report, goal), and `InteractionLog.date` is used rather than `createdAt` so a backdated log lands in the month it happened. Dormancy is deliberately **not** special-cased — a dormant pair is quiet, and quiet is already excluded. `countAdminSeats()`, `currentPeriod()` and `periodRange()` (half-open UTC month windows) ship from the same file so no caller invents its own month arithmetic; `planGate` now reads its capacity count from there too, with the capacity-vs-usage distinction written down instead of rediscovered. New `UsageRollup` model (`orgId` + `TENANT_MODELS`, unique `(orgId, metric, period)`) is the ledger a usage screen reads, so no request path ever scans seven activity tables; `src/lib/jobs/usageRollup.ts` refreshes the open month and the previous one nightly at 02:40 UTC as a plain handler that ports to the leader-elected scheduler (#1676), registered from `/api/cron/start` next to the other scheduled jobs and runnable on demand via `GET /api/cron?job=usage-rollup`. Idempotent by construction: computed metrics are written absolutely, counters are never recomputed, and `setUsage`/`recordUsage` refuse each other's metrics. Video volume is finally measured at the one room-creation chokepoint (`generateMeetingLink()`) as `VIDEO_ROOM`/`VIDEO_PARTICIPANT` so JaaS MAU exposure is a number rather than a guess — **reported, never gated**: no meeting behaviour, JaaS routing or status code changes, and the counter swallows its own failures. Definition, metric table and the deliberately-not-metered list (mentor seats, mentee seats, programmes): [docs/metering.md](docs/metering.md).
